Subject: URGENT: Production errors & latency spike in us-east-1 (AZ1)

David / Marissa —

We're seeing a sustained surge in 5xx and client-visible latency for our production traffic routed to us-east-1 (AZ1) starting ~07:50 PDT. Error rate jumped from ~0.6% to 7.8% and median p95 latency is now ~1.2s (previous baseline ~140ms). Several of our critical customers are failing health checks and our ops team is receiving pages.

We opened a ticket with support (SUP-2147) — attaching initial error snippets. Can Redwood trigger an immediate cross-region steering to us-east-2 and confirm any potential session/kv-cache impact? We need an ETA and confirmation that this will not invalidate in-flight requests. If you require exec escalation for a temporary routing override or credits, please advise.

This is impacting live billing; procurement is on standby for any change approvals.

Thanks,
Aisha
Aisha Malik
Head of Cloud Ops, OmniHealth

- Hannah (SRE) is pulling telemetry and will confirm root-cause hypothesis (kvcache saturation vs. routing fabric).
- We're pre-authorizing a controlled traffic shift to us-east-2 for OmniHealth as a mitigant; this will be done via policy override on the routing plane.

On Thu, Sep 30, 2027 at 08:22 AM David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com> wrote:
> Hannah — can you confirm expected client-visible behavior for active sessions during a geo-steer (KV cache warm vs. cold, potential transient 429s)?

Short answer: Yes, clients may observe transient increased latency and a small spike in 429s while KV caches warm in us-east-2. Based on current metrics (attached snapshot) the primary amplifier appears to be KV cache eviction in AZ1 combined with a downstream networking fanout issue to a hardware pool.

Estimated impact window for the controlled traffic shift: 8–12 minutes of elevated p95 for affected flows; most requests will succeed. We'll do staged routing (10% -> 50% -> 100%) with canary checks.

Attachments: kvcache_snapshot.png

I'll initiate the canary at T+5 unless I hear otherwise.

Hannah
